candidate_relations.reason: Malaria does not account for the 1-month indolent course, massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia pattern, and elevated liver enzymes in the absence of travel history to malaria-endemic areas; it is a separate diagnosis
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Malaria is a distinct parasitic infection; while it can cause splenomegaly and fever, it is a different diagnostic entity from visceral leishmaniasis

candidate_relations.reason: TB does not typically produce the degree of massive splenomegaly and pancytopenia seen here, and the clinical picture (hilly Nepal region, failed antibiotics, massive splenomegaly) is more consistent with visceral leishmaniasis than TB
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Tuberculosis is a bacterial infection; while it can cause fever and hepatosplenomegaly, it is a different diagnostic entity

candidate_relations.reason: Kala-Azar (Visceral Leishmaniasis) is a direct alias for the reference diagnosis. The clinical features—prolonged fever, massive splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, pancytopenia, elevated liver enzymes, hilly Nepal region, and failure of antibiotics—are classic for visceral leishmaniasis
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Kala-Azar is the common name for visceral leishmaniasis; the label explicitly states both terms

candidate_relations.reason: While histiocytosis can cause hepatosplenomegaly and cytopenias, it is a separate disease category and does not match the epidemiological and clinical profile pointing to visceral leishmaniasis in this case
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Histiocytosis is a distinct group of disorders involving histiocyte proliferation; it is a different diagnostic entity
